title: Does the Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Hint at the Multiverse's End?
excerpt:
A new analysis focuses on three worlds visible above New York.
The multiverse-collapse interpretation remains a theory, not a Marvel confirmation.
body_md:
The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has sparked a wave of speculation about the fate of Marvel's interconnected realities. One analysis focuses on a brief image of New York's skyline that may hint at the final stages of a catastrophic collision between worlds. The important distinction is between what the trailer visibly depicts and what commentators infer from those images.

At roughly 1:31 in the trailer, Steve Rogers looks toward the city from a building presumed to be Avengers Tower. Two additional worlds appear in the sky, one seemingly damaged or collapsing. The article connects this visual to the concept of an incursion, a collision of realities previously explored in the MCU's multiverse storytelling, including Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

The more dramatic interpretation is that only three worlds may remain and the wider multiverse could be approaching annihilation. That is a theory based on a short shot, not an officially confirmed plot revelation. Seeing three worlds in one frame does not establish that no other realities exist elsewhere in the story.

The analysis also suggests that the heroes may split between an offensive team traveling to the X-Men's reality and a defensive team protecting the main MCU Earth. Characters discussed in this possible arrangement include Sam Wilson, Shang-Chi, Reed Richards, Thor and Yelena Belova. Other Fantastic Four members, Wakandan forces and the Thunderbolts might remain behind. These are interpretations of trailer footage rather than an official roster of assignments.

Another speculative thread concerns Steve Rogers and the decision he made at the end of Avengers: Endgame to reunite with Peggy Carter. The article raises the possibility that his altered personal timeline could be connected to the larger crisis. Without explicit confirmation in the finished film, however, it would be misleading to declare Steve the definitive cause of the multiversal catastrophe.

Doctor Doom, portrayed by Robert Downey Jr., is expected to stand at the center of a conflict where saving one reality could threaten another. That raises a compelling moral problem: heroes from different franchises may each believe they are defending their own world. The film is scheduled for theatrical release on December 18, 2026, but the trailer alone cannot settle the multiverse's ultimate fate.
